statement: In a triangle, the largest angle is 3 times the smallest angle, and the third angle is 20 degrees more than the smallest angle. How big is the largest angle?

choices.misconception: I found the smallest angle, 32 degrees, and stopped there.
I found the middle angle, 32 + 20, instead of the largest.
I forgot the extra 20 degrees, so I shared 180 degrees into 5 equal parts of 36.
I added the 20 degrees to 180 instead of taking it away, so I shared 200 degrees into 5 parts of 40.

hints: Describe every angle using the smallest one.
The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. If the smallest angle is one part, the others are 3 parts and 1 part plus 20 degrees. Take away the 20 degrees first.
Five equal parts plus 20 degrees make 180 degrees, so five parts make 160 degrees.

solutions.reliable: Call the smallest angle one part. The other angles are 3 parts and 1 part plus 20 degrees. Altogether 5 parts plus 20 degrees make 180 degrees, so 5 parts make 160 degrees and one part is 32 degrees. The angles are 32, 52 and 96 degrees, which add up to 180, and 96 is indeed the largest. The transferable idea: express every angle through one unknown, then use the 180-degree angle sum.

whyOnTest: The triangle angle sum is tested together with careful translation: describe every angle through the smallest, then share out 180 degrees.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
